statement: For any tensor-product-closed finite binary-law family, v>=0, 0<delta<1-v, L>=0 and 0<T<=delta/4, the uniform proper-tested-set conditioning hypothesis implies Pr(W>=ceil((v+delta)n))<=exp(-delta*T*n/(16*(1+L))) at every n>=1.
hypotheses: All masses are real, nonnegative, and sum to one; coordinates may be arbitrarily correlated.
The family is closed under the explicit independently repeated product law.
Every proper tested set of positive mass with cost at most T has conditional mean at most v+delta/4.
